title: Cross-CPU portability sweep AVX2-only host vs AVX-512 host
description:
Run the `permanent_bipedal3` SIMD path on at least two CPU classes (the dev host AVX2-only AMD 5900X plus an AVX-512-capable host) and document throughput delta + correctness equivalence.

## Background

The SIMD kernel (T12) compiles both AVX2 and AVX-512 paths; the dev host has AVX2 only. Running the same binary (or rebuilt-with-`target-cpu=native`) on an AVX-512 host validates the AVX-512 code path was actually exercised somewhere and that runtime detection picks the right backend.

The AVX-512 host may be a CI runner, a researcher's workstation, or a cloud instance — document whichever is used.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] Throughput measurements exist for at least two CPU classes (AVX2-only, AVX-512-capable) at $n \in \{24, 28, 32, 36\}$.
- [ ] [hard] Correctness equivalence: same seeded inputs produce bit-identical permanents on both hosts.
- [ ] [hard] CSV at `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/s3_cross_cpu-YYYY-MM-DD.csv` records mean wall-clock per host with `lscpu` fingerprints.
- [ ] [hard] Writeup at `dev/plans/s3_cross_cpu_portability.md` exists, attached via `jit doc add`, calls out the AVX2-vs-AVX-512 throughput ratio observed and whether it confirms the AVX-512 path is exercising the wider lanes (vs falling back to AVX2 silently).
- [ ] [aspirational] AVX-512 throughput is $\ge 1.5\times$ the AVX2 throughput on the same matrix size.
